WHAT IT READS: five public GETs, each one read in its handler before this plan, by checker-94 on 2026-11-07, as writing nothing: https://narrowhighway.com/health and https://narrowhighway.tv/health (nh-engine), https://api.narrowhighway.com/health (V3, the constant ok), https://api.narrowhighway.com/mcp (nh-mcp, a fixed retry line), and https://narrowhighway.org/health (the witness app). No POST, no seal page, nothing whose handler can write, mint, attest or fetch elsewhere. A face is healthy when it answers 200 within 10 s with the body that face gives when well: the health JSON with ok true for the four health reads, and the retry line for /mcp. Each face's test is written down in the code and pinned by a test.

WHEN IT CALLS A FACE DOWN: each face is read up to three times, 20 s apart, and is down only when all three fail. One run reads the faces side by side and ends within two minutes. The schedule is every 10 minutes at minutes ending in 7, away from the top of the hour, plus a run by hand. GitHub's schedule is best effort and can run late, and GitHub turns off a public repository's schedules after 60 days with no activity in it: both are named in the workflow's header, not hidden. The watch on the box still answers a frozen engine in about two minutes; this one answers a dead box, DNS, TLS or the edge within about ten.

THE ALERT: one issue, titled 'Uptime: a public face is down', assigned to the repository owner so GitHub notifies him. When faces are down and no such issue is open, the run opens it, listing each down face with its URL, the status or error of each try, and the time. When it is already open, the run comments only when the set of down faces changes, so a long outage makes no flood. When every face reads healthy and the issue is open, the run comments that it recovered and closes it. The open issue is the only state between runs. Its text carries only public facts: no box address, no path on the box, nothing private.

HOW IT IS BUILT: tools/uptime.py, standard library only, holds the reads and a pure decision from the results and the open issue to one of open, comment, close or nothing; the calls to gh are a thin layer around that decision. .github/workflows/uptime.yml runs it on ubuntu-latest with permissions contents: read and issues: write and nothing else, the default token and no secret, a concurrency group so two runs never act at once, timeout-minutes 5, and every action pinned by a full commit SHA, since this token can write issues. It never runs on push, pull_request or pull_request_target.

RED FIRST AND TESTS: before the step nothing reads the faces from outside, and the tests fail for want of the tool. Tests run tools/uptime.py against servers the test opens on 127.0.0.1: one healthy, one answering 500, one answering 200 with a wrong body, one that never answers, one that closes at once. They show the three-try rule, the 10 s bound and the two-minute run bound, and each branch of the decision with a stub gh on PATH that records its calls: open once, comment only on a change, close on recovery, nothing when healthy and none open. A test pins the workflow file: schedule, triggers, permissions, concurrency, timeout, SHA pins, no secrets. The public-facts rule is pinned by a test that fails on any address, path or name beyond the five URLs in what the tool writes.

SHIP AND LIVE: after the checker's pass and the commit, the lead pushes master, CI runs as on every push, and the lead starts the workflow once by hand with gh. A checker reads that run's log by gh: five faces read healthy, no issue opened, and the run used no permission beyond the two. The alert path on the live side is proven only on the owner's word, since it publishes an issue in a public repository: a run by hand with an input that adds a sixth face at a closed port on the runner itself, 127.0.0.1, so no public face is touched, opens the issue and the next normal run closes it. Without that word, the record names the alert path as proven only by tests.

NAMED: it alerts and never restarts; a key to the box in a workflow would be a way in. It does not see a face that answers health while failing other reads, and it is one more reader of public /health. A runner whose own network fails can open a false issue, which the next healthy run closes; the three tries make that rare and the record counts any that occur.
goal: Something outside the box notices when a public face is down. The watch on the box restarts a frozen engine, but it dies with the box, and it cannot see DNS, TLS, the edge or the box itself. This run adds a second eye off the box: a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow in this repository reads each public face, and when a face is down it opens one issue, assigned to the owner so GitHub notifies him, and closes it when every face reads healthy again. It only reads and reports. It holds no key to the box, restarts nothing and writes nothing on any face. The owner chose it on 2026-11-07: 'Uptime then handler'.

Input: a face that fails half its reads (a crash-looping or memory-starved process). A test pins that the tool exits 0 on every path but a broken workflow file or a crash, and that no gh call is made at all.

WHAT IT READS: five public GETs, each read in its handler by checker-94 and checker-95 as writing nothing: https://narrowhighway.com/health and https://narrowhighway.tv/health (nh-engine), https://api.narrowhighway.com/health (V3), https://api.narrowhighway.com/mcp (nh-mcp, a fixed retry line), and https://narrowhighway.org/health (the witness app). One push goes out when it is called down, naming each down face, and one when it is called back. At most six pushes a day, the heartbeat aside; past that, the summary records what was not sent. Never an exception's text, a response body or a header. A test injects errors whose text carries a marker string, from the resolver, the socket and the TLS layer, and from bodies and headers, and fails if the marker reaches anything written. The ntfy topic is a repository secret, NTFY_TOPIC, and is never printed: GitHub masks it, and a test pins that the tool never writes it. The push goes by HTTPS POST to ntfy.sh with the topic in the path and plain text, with a title, a priority, and no attachment or link.

HOW IT IS BUILT: tools/uptime.py, standard library only, holds the reads, the decision and the push, with the push sender passed in so tests never reach ntfy. It runs only when github.repository is matharrismma/concordance-2, so a fork does nothing. permissions are contents: read and nothing else, and GitHub also gives every token metadata read. findings: docs/harness/runs/2026-11-07-outside-uptime.jsonl:4 NO EMAIL, BY CONSTRUCTION: 'never sends email' is not true as planned. (a) By the plan's own exception a crash exits non-zero, the run fails, and GitHub mails the user who last changed the cron line; the crash's traceback also prints exception text to the public log, outside the marker test. (b) Steps that are not the tool's (checkout during a GitHub incident, a lost runner, an invalid workflow file) fail the run, and a run ended by timeout-minutes or displaced from the concurrency queue is cancelled, which as far as I know can mail a 'Run cancelled' notice; I cannot confirm which of these the default settings send. Needed: main catches every exception, writes 'crash' and the class name only, and exits 0; checkout and cache steps carry continue-on-error; the push gets its own deadline and gaps, and the run bound is tested with a stalled sender; and the plan says plainly that only the owner's own Actions notification setting (no email) makes 'never' certain, that it is his word, and that it also silences Actions mail for his other repositories.

docs/harness/runs/2026-11-07-outside-uptime.jsonl:4 WHEN IT PUSHES: a withheld or failed push is lost for good. Input: six pushes already sent today (three short outages), then a fourth outage. It is called down, the cap withholds the push, and only the summary records it, which notifies no one. The next day nothing pushes either, because the site is already called down, so the owner never hears of an outage that may last days, and its recovery is withheld the same way. The same happens when ntfy.sh refuses all three tries. Needed: the state keeps what was last delivered beside what is called, and any run that finds them different with the cap open sends the current state; a test feeds the cap and a failing sender and sees the catch-up push.

docs/harness/runs/2026-11-07-outside-uptime.jsonl:4 WHEN IT PUSHES and SHIP AND LIVE: the alert rests on state carried between runs, and nothing planned shows it carries. Input: the restore never finds the saved file (a wrong path or key, a save step skipped, the cache service answering a miss). Every run then starts from up with no counts, the two-runs-down rule can never fire, and every run is green and silent: the watch is dead while it looks well. The live check reads one run, which cannot see this. Needed: the summary names the run whose state it restored, or says none; the live check reads two scheduled runs in a row and sees the second restore the first's state with the counts advanced; and the heartbeat says how many runs the state has carried and since when, so a reset shows on the phone.

docs/harness/runs/2026-11-07-outside-uptime.jsonl:4 WHEN IT PUSHES and NAMED: misses by design are still unnamed. A face is up in a run when one try of three answers, and the site is called down only after two down runs in a row. Input: a face down in every other run is never pushed (the plan's own 'flaps every other run' test states no expected outcome); a face that answers one read in three is up forever; and a face can be called back while it still fails most reads. A miss stays a miss: either a rule that catches these (for example, down in two of the last three runs) or NAMED lists them, and the flap test states its expected outcome.

The engine's own witness listener, the documented rollback for .org, answers /health with ok true and surface witness as well (src/concordance/web/api.py:706, with the witness listener that src/concordance/__main__.py:103 starts). Only the witness app adds a commit and a doors list (witness nh_org/serve.py:127). Input: .org rolled back to the engine while the witness app is dead reads as the witness app up. Needed: .org's test also requires the commit and doors fields, or the overlap is named as /mcp's is.

docs/harness/runs/2026-11-07-outside-uptime.jsonl:4 WHAT IT WRITES: one channel and the one credential are not covered. (a) The state file is public: a pull request's run, a fork's included, can restore caches saved on the default branch, so the marker and topic tests must cover the state file too. (b) On ntfy.sh the topic is the only credential: whoever knows it can publish to the owner's phone, links and attachments included, and read the messages ntfy.sh keeps for a while. Needed: the topic is generated at random (24 or more characters from a secure generator), never chosen by hand, and the owner is told that a push carrying a link did not come from the watch. Also, as I know ntfy.sh's documentation (not checked online), its limits count per visitor address and GitHub's runners share addresses, so an occasional refused push is expected; the catch-up rule in the second finding covers it.

A test injects errors whose text carries a marker string, from the resolver, the socket and the TLS layer, and from bodies and headers, and fails if the marker reaches anything written. The cached state file holds only these public facts, since a pull request's run can restore caches saved on the default branch, so the marker test covers it too. The ntfy topic is a repository secret, NTFY_TOPIC, and is never written: not in the push text, the summary, the log, the state, or the text of an error, since only the error's class name is written. GitHub masks it as well, and a test pins that the tool never writes it. The push goes by HTTPS POST to ntfy.sh with the topic in the path and plain text, with a title, a priority, and no attachment, link or click action, so a push carrying a link did not come from the watch. Each push attempt has a deadline of 10 s enforced from outside, and a refused push is tried twice more. Titles and every header are ASCII only, since http.client refuses anything else in a header; the body is UTF-8. The push text passes through ntfy.sh and Apple's or Google's push service to the phone, and carries only public facts.

HOW IT IS BUILT: tools/uptime.py, standard library only, holds the reads, the decision and the push. The real sender takes its base URL as a parameter, https://ntfy.sh in the workflow, and tests run that same sender against a stand-in for ntfy.sh on 127.0.0.1: they check the method, the path, ASCII-only headers with the title and priority, the body, the 10 s deadline against a stand-in that never answers, the retries, and that a refusal or a timeout leaves the push owed. A test feeds a title holding non-ASCII text and shows the sender still sends. Tests make no network call beyond 127.0.0.1. .github/workflows/uptime.yml triggers on schedule and workflow_dispatch only, every 10 minutes at minutes ending in 7. It runs only when github.repository is matharrismma/concordance-2, so a fork does nothing. permissions are contents: read and nothing else, and GitHub also gives every token metadata read. Checkout has persist-credentials false, every step is continue-on-error with its own timeout as above, checkout's own cleanup at the end of the job, which continue-on-error may not cover, does next to nothing with persist-credentials false and is named, every action is pinned by a full commit SHA, there is no concurrency group, so two runs can overlap, one started by hand or a delayed scheduled run beside the next; both restore the same state, the later save wins, and the worst case is a duplicate push, which a decision test shows by feeding two runs from one restored state, the User-Agent names the repository, and the only secret is NTFY_TOPIC. Every line the tool writes to the job summary it also prints to the run log, since the log is what gh run view --log can read. A test pins the file. Without the secret, a run reads and records and pushes nothing, and says so in the summary.

GITHUB'S SCHEDULE, STATED IN FULL in the workflow's header: scheduled runs can be delayed under load, most of all at the top of the hour, and some queued runs may be dropped, so ten minutes is the best case and not a bound; and GitHub turns off a public repository's schedules after 60 days with no activity, which the heartbeat would show as silence. ntfy.sh is a third party with its own rate limits, counted as far as known per sending address, and runners share addresses, so a push can be refused; it is retried and then owed, as above. It shares nothing with the box. Whether GitHub sends a notice before turning schedules off is not known here, and is named. The watch on the box still answers a frozen engine in about two minutes. This one answers a dead box, DNS, TLS or the edge in about twenty, since it needs two runs.

SHIP AND LIVE: after the checker's pass and the commit, the lead pushes master, and CI runs as on every push. The topic is the only credential ntfy.sh has: on the owner's word for that touch, either he sets it himself on GitHub's website, or the lead generates it with secrets.token_urlsafe(24), 32 characters ntfy accepts, passes it to gh secret set on stdin and never as an argument, and gives it to the owner in this session to subscribe in the ntfy app. It goes into no repository file, ledger line, commit or report; this session's transcript on the laptop will hold it, and the record names that. The lead then starts the workflow once by hand, and a checker reads, by gh run view --log, that run and the two scheduled runs after it: five faces read healthy, nothing pushed but a heartbeat if the check spans Monday 13:00 UTC, each scheduled run names, by run id, the run whose state it restored, and that is the newest run that finished before it, judged by run ids since two runs can overlap, the state carried, and the token's permissions as stated. The drill runs only on the owner's word: a run by hand with the yes-or-no input drill set to yes adds one fixed sixth face at a closed port on the runner, 127.0.0.1:9, so no public face is touched, sends one push marked as a drill, skips the two-of-three rule, and leaves the saved state alone, so it proves the push path only. The owner says whether it reached his phone, since only he can see that, and the record quotes him. Without his word, the record names the push path as proven only by tests.

NAMED: it alerts and never restarts; a key to the box in a workflow would be a way in. It does not see a face that answers health while failing other reads, and it is one more reader of public /health. A failure of the runner's own network in two runs of three could push a false alarm; the heartbeat counts those each week, as above.
goal: Something outside the box notices when a public face is down, and tells the owner by a push to his phone. The watch on the box restarts a frozen engine, but it dies with the box, and it cannot see DNS, TLS, the edge or the box itself. This run adds a second eye off the box: a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow in this repository reads each public face, and when a face stays down it sends one push through ntfy, a free push service that needs no account, and one more when every face is back. It only reads and reports. It holds no key to the box, restarts nothing, writes nothing on any face, opens no issue, and never sends email. The owner chose it: 'Uptime then handler' (2026-11-07), and on 2026-11-08 'I don't want emails sent' and 'Push is preferred'. Plan two answered line 3 by dropping issues; plan three answered line 5, plan four answered line 7, and plan five answers line 9, keeping the design.
